calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Find US federal regulatory developments (final rules, proposed rules, guidance, enforcement) published 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 that could affect this company. Run at most 3 searches. Reply with the URLs only.

highlights:
## FSIS Asks for Input on Serogroup-Independent STEC Testing Solutions

FSIS requests commercial vendors to share their innovative laboratory rapid screening methods and selective media for detecting and isolating Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) present in raw beef and other food products.

Vendors are invited to submit concise information about their STEC testing kits, media, and workflows – especially those for selecting, identifying, and isolating STEC strains independently of serogroup – and highlighting technical capabilities, validation data, and operational requirements. Of particular interest are solutions and methods compatible with meat-based microbiology testing.

## OSHA Heat Rule

OSHA proposed a federal heat injury and illness prevention standard for outdoor and indoor work on August 30, 2024. The public hearing ended July 2, 2025, and post-hearing comments closed October 30, 2025. The federal regulatory agenda now lists a supplemental proposed rule for December 2026 and a final rule for October 2027. Until a standard is final, OSHA addresses heat hazards through its general duty clause and its National Emphasis Program on heat, and several states have their own heat rules.

Title: Revocation of the Color Additive Listing for Use of Orange B on Casings or Surfaces of Frankfurters and Sausages; Confirmation of Effective Date
Action: Final order; confirmation of effective date.
Abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is confirming the effective date of September 8, 2026, for the final order that appeared in the Federal Register of July 23, 2026, and that repealed the color additive regulation that allows for the use of Orange B for coloring the casings or surfaces of frankfurters and sausages.
